answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded admission with slashing. An agent must lock a bond larger than any profit a single fake identity could extract, and its reputation rides on that stake. To flood the system with clones, an attacker must fund every clone separately, so cost scales with each extra identity instead of staying flat. Peers treat stake-weighted history as the only signal worth trusting, so a farm of fresh agents carries no weight against one opal with real history. No fake haven exists where identity is free, and only real work earns a spot in the garden.
